Standard: The full or partial pressure suit and associated plumbing, regulator, and tubing used for altitude protection is in compliance with AIR-STD-1052 Ed 2 v1, Physiological Criteria paragraph for the normal and emergency envelopes of the air vehicle. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Inspect air vehicle and oxygen system specifications to ensure all operational phases are accounted for in the altitude protection system hardware.
(2) Examine component hardware configuration documents are inspected to confirm compliance with hardware drawings. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Test the man-mounted altitude protection components to ensure their functional performance in conjunction with the breathing system, including failure mechanisms, to ensure all failure modes are identified and to establish reliability.
  (2) Lab test: Test the altitude protection of the pressure suit throughout the air vehicle envelope in an altitude chamber to verify the approved pressure schedule and include failure modes and mechanisms to verify alert annunciation.
  (3) Lab test: Accomplish testing in an altitude chamber with breathing machine and head forms and human subjects, using the air vehicle’s breathing system.
  (4) Lab test: Test pressure suits IAW the approved pressure schedules and verify that the lower portion of the altitude garment always inflates in advance or concurrently with the upper portion of the altitude garment.
  (5) Lab test: Verify that the pressure suits provide adequate ventilation and thermal management. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
  (6) Flight test: Conduct flight tests to verify compliance with the approved pressure schedule.
